name: Lagos
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Lagos: counterparty and trade diligence, property title checks and support for Lagos disputes and recovery.
hero_lede: Lagos is Nigeria's commercial capital, home to its main ports, banks, stock exchange and much of its manufacturing. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, working with Nigerian counsel and qualified local professionals where on-the-ground enquiries are needed.
intro: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria and the centre of its private economy. Although Abuja is the federal capital, most of the country's banks, insurers, manufacturers, trading houses and professional firms are based in Lagos, and the state is often estimated to generate around a third of national GDP. Its seaports at Apapa and Tin Can Island, joined more recently by the Lekki Deep Sea Port and the Lekki Free Zone to the east, handle a large share of Nigeria's imports. Industrial estates at Ikeja and Agbara host food, pharmaceutical and consumer goods production, and Murtala Muhammed International Airport is a principal gateway to West Africa.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Lagos because large sums move through counterparties whose ownership and track record can be hard to confirm from abroad. Importers, distributors and agents may operate through several entities; fintech and payments companies grow quickly and change hands; and prime real estate on Lagos Island, Ikoyi, Victoria Island and Lekki has been the subject of disputed allocations and title fraud. Foreign creditors and investors pursuing recovery need to know which assets are real and reachable. Lagos also has its own courts, an established court-connected dispute resolution centre and a state land registry, all of which shape how evidence is gathered.

matters.title: Importer, distributor and agent checks
matters.text: Lagos importers and distributors often trade through several related companies. We review Corporate Affairs Commission records, litigation, media and regulatory sources to identify owners, directors and related parties, and to test whether a partner has the operations, licences and reputation it claims before a client appoints or pays it.

matters.title: Property title and allocation risk
matters.text: Land on Lagos Island, Ikoyi, Victoria Island and Lekki carries a history of competing claims and disputed allocations. Working with Nigerian counsel, we help clients verify title documents, Governor's consent history and litigation affecting a property before purchase, lending or acceptance as security.

matters.title: Fintech and payments counterparties
matters.text: Lagos is the centre of Nigeria's fintech sector, where companies scale quickly and ownership shifts through funding rounds. We examine corporate history, principals, regulatory actions, litigation and media to identify undisclosed affiliates, prior failures or enforcement history before partnership, investment or onboarding.

matters.title: Trade and port-related fraud
matters.text: Shipments through Apapa, Tin Can Island and Lekki involve clearing agents, consignees and logistics firms that can be used for document fraud or diversion. We trace the companies and individuals behind a transaction and test whether goods, warehouses and counterparties exist as described.

matters.title: Asset tracing for Lagos recovery
matters.text: Creditors with judgments or awards against Lagos-based debtors need a realistic picture of reachable assets. We map companies, property interests and connected parties from public sources and local enquiries so Nigerian counsel can plan registration, enforcement or freezing applications in the Lagos courts.

local_context.title: Courts in Lagos
local_context.text: The High Court of Lagos State hears most commercial disputes in the state and has used dedicated commercial divisions. In 2025 the Lagos State Government unveiled a new Commercial Court building of the High Court at Tapa, Lagos Island, with the Governor describing it as intended to speed business dispute resolution; a revenue court for tax and land use charge matters was announced alongside it. The Federal High Court also sits in Lagos and has jurisdiction over matters such as companies, banking, admiralty and federal revenue.

local_context.title: Lagos Multi-Door Courthouse
local_context.text: The Lagos Multi-Door Courthouse (LMDC), established in 2002 and now governed by the Lagos Multi-Door Courthouse Law 2015, is described as the first court-connected alternative dispute resolution centre in Africa. It offers mediation, arbitration, conciliation, early neutral evaluation and hybrid processes, and the courts can refer cases to it. Lagos also hosts the Lagos Court of Arbitration and many arbitrations seated in the city under Nigerian arbitration legislation.

local_context.title: Land and property records
local_context.text: Land in Lagos State is administered by the state government, and transfers of interests generally require the Governor's consent under the Land Use Act. Title documents such as certificates of occupancy are recorded at the Lagos State Lands Registry. In 2025 press reports described an EFCC investigation, at the records-request stage, into alleged irregular allocations of prime land in Lagos; these remained allegations. Searches at the registry are normally conducted by Nigerian counsel or surveyors.

local_context.title: Registries and regulators
local_context.text: Companies are registered nationally with the Corporate Affairs Commission, which has offices in Lagos, so corporate searches are not Lagos-specific. The Nigerian Exchange, Nigeria's principal stock exchange, is headquartered in Lagos, while the Securities and Exchange Commission and Central Bank of Nigeria are headquartered in Abuja. The EFCC operates zonal directorates in Lagos, which handle many financial crime investigations involving businesses in the city.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Lagos and works on Lagos matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client and its Nigerian counsel first, whether a distributor appointment, an acquisition, a property transaction or recovery of a judgment or award, and scope the work to it. Desk research covers Corporate Affairs Commission filings, Lagos and federal court records available through counsel, NGX disclosures, media and regulatory sources. Land searches, court file reviews and site verification are carried out by qualified local professionals instructed with counsel. We do not seek bank, telecoms or police records outside lawful process. Reports state sources and confidence levels.

faqs.q: Can a Lagos property title be verified before purchase?
faqs.a: Yes, through searches at the Lagos State Lands Registry and enquiries into Governor's consent history, survey plans and litigation. These searches are conducted by Nigerian counsel or surveyors. We coordinate them with background research on the seller and any intermediaries, because title disputes in Lagos often involve competing claims and documents that appear valid on their face.

faqs.q: Where are commercial disputes heard in Lagos?
faqs.a: Most commercial disputes are heard by the High Court of Lagos State, which unveiled a dedicated Commercial Court building on Lagos Island in 2025. Companies, banking and admiralty matters within federal jurisdiction go to the Federal High Court, Lagos. The Lagos Multi-Door Courthouse and arbitration offer alternatives. Counsel chooses the forum.

faqs.q: Can you check a Lagos company that trades through several entities?
faqs.a: Yes. We search Corporate Affairs Commission records for each entity, compare directors, shareholders, addresses and filing histories, and add litigation, media and regulatory sources to identify common control. Where documents are incomplete or inconsistent, local verification of addresses and operations can be arranged with qualified professionals.

faqs.q: Is it possible to trace assets in Lagos for an award obtained abroad?
faqs.a: Often. We identify companies, property and business interests connected to the debtor from public sources and local enquiries. Recognition and enforcement are matters for Nigerian counsel, who will advise on the appropriate court. Our research helps counsel decide whether enforcement is worthwhile and which assets to target first.

faqs.q: Do Lagos free zone companies need different checks?
faqs.a: Free zone enterprises in the Lekki and Lagos free zones are licensed under the free zone regime rather than registered only with the Corporate Affairs Commission. We confirm licensing status where possible, identify owners and promoters, and review media and litigation, coordinating local enquiries where zone records are not publicly accessible.
